title: Autotune: Cache Key Recommendation Engine & Safe Apply for KV Prefix TTLs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a recommendation engine that suggests safe, workload-aware KV/prefix caching configs (cache key patterns, TTL buckets, and eviction hints) and an automated safe-apply rollout path with fast rollback. This ticket covers modeling hit-rate impacts from alternate keying strategies, defining TTL policy families, integrating telemetry for decision making, and implementing canary-aware config apply logic with staged metrics gates.

Motivation: Prefix-aware caching has large cost upside on high-reuse workloads but is brittle when keys are too coarse or TTLs are mis-sized. Right now teams manually tune policies per service, causing inconsistent economics and occasional cache pollution that increases token spend. An autotune engine will accelerate safe wins and reduce manual ops by recommending changes and providing a controlled apply/rollback mechanism integrated with Console telemetry and runtime feature flags.

Scope:
- Hit-rate modeling: offline simulator that consumes prefix frequency histograms and request traces to estimate hit-rate, miss-cost, and tail latency delta for candidate key designs.
- TTL policy families: propose a small set of TTL buckets and decay rules (e.g., adaptive TTL based on prefix popularity tiers + safety floor) and quantify expected cost savings/regressions.
- Cache key design heuristics: canonicalization rules (tokenization boundaries, function-call separators, user-id scoping) and rules to avoid high-cardinality collapse.
- Safe apply/rollback: staged rollout orchestration with micro-canary cohorts, realtime SLO and cost gating, automatic rollback on regression, and human override.
- Integration: Console suggestions UI, an API endpoint for suggestions, and a background job that runs simulations nightly.

Out of scope for this ticket: full autosync apply to customer-configured Dedicated clusters (we will provide PRs/patches and operator-run docs in a follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Offline simulator can ingest a 7-day prefix histogram and produce per-candidate hit-rate, expected token-savings, and estimated latency impact in under 30 minutes for a medium-sized dataset.
A recommended TTL family (3-5 buckets) and cache-key canonicalization preview is produced for a sample workload with expected costs and risk summary.

A safe-apply workflow exists that can run a staged rollout to 1% -> 10% -> 50% traffic cohorts with automated metric gates (error rate, 95p latency, token cost) and abort/rollback behavior documented.
Console shows suggestion entries with links to simulation artifacts and a one-click ‘start safe apply’ that creates a rollout job record in Console.
E2E tests simulate a regression and validate that the rollback path cancels the rollout and reverts config within the target SLA (<= 2 minutes to cancel and initiate rollback action).
Design doc and runbook for operators are published and peer-reviewed by Reliability and Security teams.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket. Initial scoping call with Marco, Leila (Reliability), and Tomas (Console). Decided to prototype offline simulator first and keep apply/rollback as a separate plumbed state machine that interacts with existing rollout infra.

2026-03-04 - Marco Rivera: Prototype simulator ingestion completed. Using compressed prefix histograms from request logs. Early results show 8-18% token reduction on two sampled services with conservative TTL buckets.

2026-03-06 - Leila Mendoza (Reliability): Concern raised about canary cohort isolation for stateful caches. Action: add KV version-tagging and a fast-read-path that can prefer previous policy if anomalies detected.

2026-03-08 - Design review: Aisha and Marco presented keying heuristics. Feedback to avoid user-id concatenation without explicit opt-in; add entropy threshold metric to detect dangerous key collapse.
2026-03-10 - Marco Rivera: Implemented rollout job API and metric gate hooks. Added automatic abort on >20% regression in token spend among canary cohort vs control. Pending integration tests.
2026-03-11 - Tomas Ivanov (Console): UI mockups uploaded. Suggestion entries will include ‘Risk score’ and link to simulation CSV. Need new API field for human-explanation text.
rollout_plan: 1) Nightly simulator generates candidate suggestions and stores artifacts. 2) Suggestion appears in Console with a risk score and one-click start. 3) Start safe-apply creates a rollout job: 1% traffic (24h), evaluate gates; if pass -> 10% (24h); if pass -> 50% (48h); final -> 100% (monitor 72h). Immediate automatic rollback triggers on gate failure; on success an audit entry and optional scheduler to auto-promote after window. Manual abort allowed at any stage.
risk_assessment: Primary risks: accidental key coarsening causing cache stampede or privacy leakage, mis-sized TTLs causing stale outputs, and incorrect accounting that underestimates cost regressions. Mitigations: entropy threshold checks, per-prefix cardinality caps, TTL safety floors, version-tagging for easy revert, conservative default TTLs, and mandatory human approval for high-risk suggestions.
test_plan: Unit tests for simulator components, integration tests that run a simulated request stream with known prefixes and validate predicted vs observed hit-rate within a 5% error margin, E2E tests exercising the rollout job and automated rollback, and chaos test that simulates partial infra failures during rollout to ensure safe-apply does not leave partially applied configs.
notes: We will prioritize supporting HTTP-based inference endpoints first (text-gen/chat) and add embeddings/cross-request use cases in a subsequent iteration. Coordinate with Security for a quick review of any telemetry that includes user-scoped prefixes.
